# AI Deflection

`customer_support.knowledge_and_deflection.ai_deflection` · v0.1.0 · **draft** · **STUB**

**Can a model answer this safely, and does it know when to stop trying?**


> Putting a model between the question and the queue, and owning what it says. The failure that matters is not the occasional wrong answer — it is that a confident wrong answer costs more than no answer at all, because the customer acts on it and returns with a second problem plus a grievance, and the transcript is now evidence. The operator judgement is about handover and grounding: when the assistant must escalate without being asked, what it may assert versus what it must cite, and whether a conversation it contained was actually resolved or merely outlasted. Containment is the number the vendor sells; it is not the number to run the programme on.

This is the capability most likely to be promoted for the wrong reason — a vendor demo rather than a queue reading — so it deliberately stays a stub until self_service_deflection's measurement discipline exists to inherit, because an AI deflection programme built on an unaudited containment metric inherits every failure mode of the human one and adds fabrication to it.
